steps.body: Whatever the story, the question "how many are left?" always asks about what remains.
steps.narration: Whatever the story, the question "how many are left?" always asks about what remains.

widget.prompt: 10 balloons float away until 4 have gone. Hop back to show how many are left.

commonLandings.feedback: That counts the balloons that floated away, not the ones still held.

widget.missFeedback: Start at 10 and count back 4: you land on 6.
widget.successFeedback: Landed on 6 — 10 balloons with 4 gone leaves 6.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents koa how many left.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for koa how many left must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines koa how many left.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

steps.body: Track each balloon with a finger.
explanationVariants: Each balloon that floats away is one fewer held.

widget.prompt: 10 balloons float away one at a time until 4 have gone. How many balloons are left?

That is the starting number. 4 have gone since then.

explanationVariants: Fold down one finger for each of the 5 balloons that leaves; 3 fingers stay up.
The fingers still up model the balloons that remain.

widget.prompt: Show 8 fingers to stand for the balloons. Fold down 5 fingers, one at a time. How many fingers stay up?

commonErrors.feedback: That counts the folded fingers, which model balloons that left. Count the fingers still up.
That is how many fingers were up before any balloons left. Five fingers must fold down.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Hold up 8 fingers. Fold down 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Three fingers stay up.
widget.successFeedback: Correct — 3 fingers stay up, so 3 balloons are left.

explanationVariants: Jo counted the 3 balloons that left instead of the 6 balloons that remain.
Nine balloons split into 3 gone and 6 still held.

widget.prompt: Jo holds 9 balloons. Then 3 float away. Jo says 3 are left. How many balloons does Jo really hold?

commonErrors.feedback: That repeats Jo's mistake. Three balloons are gone; count the other balloons still held.
That is the number before any balloons leave. The held group becomes smaller.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Draw 9 balloon loops and cross out 3. The 6 plain loops are still held.
widget.successFeedback: Correct — Jo counted what was gone; 6 balloons are really left.

steps.body: Write a sentence for a new object story.
explanationVariants: Two kites leave a group of 7, so the matching sentence is 7 minus 2 equals 5.
Changing balloons to kites does not change the take-away relationship.

widget.prompt: 7 kites fly in the sky. Then 2 kites land. Which number sentence shows how many stay in the sky?

options.feedback: Correct. Begin with 7 kites and take away the 2 that land, leaving 5 in the sky.
A plus sign would show 2 more kites joining the sky. These 2 kites land and leave.
The story starts with 7 kites, so the sentence must start with 7.
The minus sign is right, but two fewer than 7 is 5, not 6.

hints: Start with the 7 kites in the sky.
The 2 landing kites leave the sky group.

explanationVariants: Six balloons with 2 covered leave 4 balloons showing.
Cover the balloons that leave, then count only what you can still see.

widget.prompt: Draw 6 balloons. Cover 2 balloons with your hand. How many balloons can you still see?

commonErrors.feedback: That counts the balloons under your hand. Count the balloons you can still see.
That is how many you drew before covering 2. Look again at the visible group.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Cover 2 of the 6 balloon drawings. Touch the 4 drawings that are still visible.
